hints: Focus on what each axis of a Boltzmann distribution must show, energy along the bottom and count of molecules up the side.
Notice point X lines across from $E_A$ on the curve to the vertical axis, so it reads the height of the curve at that one energy.
Notice point Y lines across from the top of the peak, so think about what the highest point means for how many molecules share that energy.
walkthrough:
**Recall the axes of the Boltzmann curve**

Remember this is a friendly distribution plot. The horizontal axis is energy and the vertical axis is number of molecules with a given energy.

$$\text{x-axis} = \text{energy}, \quad \text{y-axis} = \text{number of molecules}$$

**Interpret point X at $E_A$**

Point X is the y-value of the curve when energy equals $E_A$. That height tells you how many molecules have exactly that energy, not the total area beyond it.

$$\text{point X} = \text{height at } E_A = \text{number with energy } = E_A$$

**Interpret point Y at the peak**

Point Y is the y-value at the very top of the curve. The peak is where the most molecules share the same energy, so Y is that largest number of molecules.

$$\text{peak height} = \text{most probable population}$$

**Combine to choose**

Both X and Y are on the vertical axis, so both must be numbers of molecules. X is the number with energy equal to $E_A$ and Y is the largest number with the same energy.

options.A: Correct. The vertical axis is number of molecules. The height at $E_A$ gives the number with energy equal to $E_A$, and the peak height gives the largest number of molecules sharing the same energy.
options.B: Incorrect. The number with energy equal to or greater than $E_A$ is the area under the curve to the right of $E_A$, not the height at $E_A$. Point X is only the height, so this confuses height with area.
options.C: Incorrect. Point Y is on the vertical axis, so it must be a number of molecules, not an energy value. The amount of energy of the greatest number of molecules would be read off the horizontal axis at the peak.
options.D: Incorrect on both parts. Point X confuses curve height with area under the curve, and point Y confuses the vertical number scale with the horizontal energy scale.
